overview.description: Professional reglazing and refinishing of bathroom tile, bathtubs, and showers. Includes surface preparation, repair, priming, epoxy or urethane coating, and curing. A cost-effective alternative to full tile replacement.

materials.name: Professional Epoxy Coating
materials.durability: Good — lasts 10-15 years with proper care, resistant to water and mild chemicals
materials.maintenanceLevel: Low — avoid abrasive cleaners, use non-slip mats in tubs

materials.name: Urethane Topcoat System
materials.durability: Very Good — harder finish than epoxy, better scratch resistance
materials.maintenanceLevel: Low — more durable than epoxy, same care requirements

materials.name: Acid-Etch Primer
materials.durability: N/A — preparation step that ensures coating adhesion

materials.name: Fiberglass Repair Compound
materials.durability: Good — fills chips, cracks, and surface damage before coating

techniques.name: Professional Spray-On Reglazing
techniques.description: Full surface preparation (acid etch, sand, prime) followed by HVLP spray application of 3-4 coats of epoxy or urethane. Professional equipment ensures even coverage and smooth finish. Cures in 24-48 hours.
techniques.difficultyLevel: Professional only — requires ventilation and specialized equipment

techniques.name: Bathtub-Only Reglazing
techniques.description: Standard bathtub refinishing. Strip old finish, repair chips/cracks with fiberglass compound, acid-etch surface, apply bonding agent and 3-4 topcoats. Takes ~4 hours application. Costs $350-$600 for standard tub, $400-$1,400 for clawfoot.

techniques.name: Tub + Surround Reglazing
techniques.description: Combined bathtub and surrounding tile wall refinishing. Both surfaces prepped, primed, and coated to match. Costs $800-$1,200 for tub and tile surround together.

techniques.name: Tile-Only Refinishing
techniques.description: Reglaze wall or floor tile without replacing. Works on ceramic, porcelain, and some natural stone. Changes color and seals surface. Costs $4-$12 per square foot.

techniques.name: Grout Line Refinishing
techniques.description: Clean, repair, and seal grout lines as part of tile reglazing. Grout can be color-matched to new tile coating or contrasted for design effect.

patterns.name: Solid Color Refresh
patterns.description: Single uniform color across all reglazed surfaces. White is most popular (90% of reglazing jobs), followed by almond, bisque, and gray.

patterns.name: Two-Tone (Tub + Tile Contrast)
patterns.description: Different but coordinating colors for tub and tile surround. Creates visual interest without full renovation.

patterns.name: Vintage Restoration
patterns.description: Match original period colors for clawfoot tubs and vintage tile. Custom color matching available from most professional services.

climateConsiderations: Ventilation requirements during reglazing — coatings require well-ventilated space during cure

Humidity affects cure time — summer reglazing may need dehumidifier during curing
